chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, who said: A trustworthy companion of mine narrated to me that he asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام

about a man who comes upon a small amount of water on the road and wishes to perform ghusl, while he has no vessel with him and the water is in a depression; if he performs ghusl, the water from his washing will return into the water. What should he do? He عليه السلام said: "He should sprinkle one handful in front of him, one handful behind him, one handful to his right, and one handful to his left, then perform ghusl."
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', who said:

I wrote to the one who is asked about a pond in which rainwater gathers and from which water is drawn from a well; a person cleans himself in it from urine, or a junub performs ghusl in it. What is its limit beyond which it is not permissible? He wrote: "Do not perform wudu (ablution) from the like of this except out of necessity for it."

key_terms.ضَرُورَةٍ: necessity, a condition permitting restricted use
key_terms.وَهْدَةٍ: a depression in the ground where water collects
key_terms.يَسْتَنْجِي: to cleanse oneself after relieving oneself
key_terms.ٱلْجُنُبُ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.ٱلْغَدِيرِ: a pond or small pool of collected water
key_terms.ٱلْمَاءِ ٱلْقَلِيلِ: a small quantity of water with legal implications for taharah (ritual purity)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing ghusl or wudu (ablution) with a small or contaminated body of water?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses rulings concerning a small quantity of water used for purification. It explains how one should perform ghusl when standing water is limited and indicates that wudu (ablution) from a pond contaminated by human use should only be done in a case of necessity.
